She could be damaged easily. If she remained in the bloodstream for too long, the antigens could degrade her spinal cord and the proxy body would die. What had caused the older lacerations?

She darted for the nervous interface on the secretion organ. She had to get bac k into ship’s brain. She couldn't let these memories be lost when she was reinitiated. She couldn't let herself go through memory sleep again. She'd done this before, she thought. She’d been here and fought this fight. How many times? The memory damage was extensive. She must be stuck ina cycle of rebirth, fighting, rebirth. How long had this infection been here? How many times had she fought it?

For the first time, she considered her own survival apart from the survival of the ship, the completion of the mission. Her proxy body was coming apart, and she flailed, trying to connect to the interface. If she didn’t, she would repeat this over and over, degrading further each time. Then, she would be dead and so -28- would the memories of Manchu, Jurchen, Ol Cemet...and Celtiberian. She felt she had to protect those memories, though she did not know why.

The nerves were badly damaged, but she could still access the ship’s brain. She calculated that the ship would succumb to infection long before it reached the home systems. If she stayed out here to fight, the ship might make it. But she would not, It was selfish even to consider her own survival when the mission was at stake, and so close to completion. She was charged with bringing the news of Earth back to humanity. She was not charged with bringing back her own memories. There was no need for the survival of her affinity...her love—for Celtiberian. She had to communicate the location of Earth so that humanity could find what it had lost.

During a period in late April when the birds’ songs were seemingly more melodic and the glaze of sunshine inspired everyone to roost, my best friend Wallbacher was besieged by a transmogrifying lust for companionship. When his efforts fell short, he tortured himself in the face of unrequited love. His phone call early that Saturday morning had unraveled me from the drowsy warmth of my beautifully petite girlfriend Samantha; my hand numb underneath her, strapped against her belly with the elastic of her panties. Wallbacher spoke between long, contemplative silences, which he had done many times before when troubled by something. He spoke terse statements about nothing of consequence, keeping a safe distance from the underlying topic. I felt my hand tingle, the blood rushing into it. Sam rolled over in the bed and I studied the curve of her spine while the cold tickled against my skin like a feather and goose bumps Popped down my arms. Sam moaned and rolled over in bed. Why is it that as we age, we try to drift away from home? All of my friends were married or had fled to some distant town.
